absorbed: tools/audit/pile.py's duplicate/fork detection (doc_groups + skill_groups), used as-is via its scan --out JSONL manifest, invoked from tools/repoclear/scan.py duplicate_counts(); no pile.py code was copied into scan.py. alternatives.cost: Zero: already in the repo, already depended on. repoclear shells out to it rather than re-implementing it.
alternatives.covers: The entire duplicate half: byte-identical document groups with a stated survivor rule (prefer docs/, then shallowest, then alphabetical), cross-tree skill groups split into identical (safe to collapse) versus forked (needs a human decision), protected basenames so identical bytes at a runtime path (dot-codex/AGENTS.md vs root CLAUDE.md) are placement, not waste. Has its own selftest and mutation spec (4 of 4 caught). Verified live 2026-11-07: scan runs in 0.75s on this tree and reports 59 rows.
alternatives.gap: Deliberately a manifest, not a gate: no check mode that fails on growth (its --strict fails only while any fork is unresolved, which is 38 forks on main today and therefore unusable as a gate), no empty-dir detection (it works from git ls-files, and git never tracks an empty directory), no tracked-artifact detection, no stale-destination detection. It also has no baseline concept: every run reports the whole backlog, so a gate wired to it would be red until the backlog is gone rather than red only on new rot.
alternatives.maturity: In-repo since 2026-08-06, selftest + mutation spec green, run in CI falsifiability. NOT re-verified beyond the 2026-11-07 run above.
alternatives.name: tools/audit/pile.py (in-repo) -- duplicate and fork manifest

alternatives.cost: A new binary dependency plus install on every runner, in a repo that is stdlib-Python-only end to end. The gate domain would shell out to it the way repoclear shells out to pile.py, so the wiring cost is comparable; the cost is the dependency, not the code.
alternatives.covers: The strongest single alternative: one tool finds duplicate files and directories, empty files and directories (including nested), and broken symlinks, with machine-readable JSON output (-o json) and a stated policy that it will not delete anything itself. Verified from its documentation 2026-11-07 (rmlint.readthedocs.io tutorial and manpage): lint types include duplicates, duplicatedirs, emptyfiles, emptydirs; -o json streams a JSON document with header/footer statistics.
alternatives.gap: Filesystem walk, not git-aware: it reports whatever is on disk, including ignored and untracked noise (.venv, node_modules, target/), so a gate wired to it needs an exclusion list that duplicates what the repo already maintains per tool, and it would report a worktree's contents as this tree's. No skill-fork semantics: byte-identical versus diverged is the distinction pile.py exists to make, and rmlint cannot make it. No protected basenames: it would flag dot-codex/AGENTS.md as a duplicate of the root CLAUDE.md, the exact proposal pile.py's first run made and its guard now refuses. No baseline ratchet and no stale-destination check: the 2026-07-27 prompt defect (~/docs/research/) is not a duplicate or an empty dir, so rmlint cannot see it at all. And it is a C binary: adopting it adds a build/install step on the self-hosted runner for a check that runs in under 2 seconds of stdlib Python.
alternatives.maturity: Verified 2026-11-07 from documentation only (manpages.debian.org, rmlint.readthedocs.io 2.11.0): I did NOT install or run rmlint, so its JSON shape against THIS tree and its behaviour on the payload trees are unverified. Release cadence NOT verified.
alternatives.name: rmlint (sahib/rmlint, 2.11.0) -- duplicate files/dirs, empty files/dirs, broken symlinks, JSON output

alternatives.cost: A new binary dependency for less coverage than rmlint. Zero if already installed; NOT verified installed on this machine or the runner.
alternatives.covers: Duplicate files by size, then partial and full hashes, then byte-by-byte comparison; prints groups of matching files. Verified from the jdupes manpage 2026-11-07 (manpages.ubuntu.com, manpages.debian.org): -m summarizes, -S shows sizes, -R recurses.
alternatives.gap: Duplicates only: no empty dirs, no duplicate directories, no JSON output (text groups separated by blank lines), no baseline, no gate wiring, no stale destinations. A strictly weaker rmlint for this job, kept on the list because it is the textbook answer to 'find duplicates' and the reason to prefer rmlint over it (empty dirs + JSON) is a real decision, not an omission.
alternatives.maturity: Long-established; jdupes copyright 2015-2023 per its manpage. Release cadence NOT verified.

alternatives.cost: A Rust binary or Docker image, or a GitHub Action. Free. But it answers a different question, so adopting it would leave the stale-destination detector to be built anyway.
alternatives.covers: Checks links in local files (lychee . recursively, --offline blocks network requests), with a GitHub Action for CI. Verified from its docs 2026-11-07 (lychee.cli.rs getting-started, docs.rs lychee-lib 0.17.0).
alternatives.gap: It resolves LINKS. The prompts' destinations are bare prose paths (Output lands in ~/docs/research/), not Markdown link syntax, so lychee would not extract them at all: the same gap the tools-audit prior-art record names for pointers.py's doc-ref class, where lychee plus a grep only partially covers bare ~/.claude paths in prose. It also has no duplicate, empty-dir, artifact, or baseline concept, and no notion of a destination directory (it checks whether a link is accessible, not whether the directory a file would land in exists).
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained on the evidence found (current docs site, published Docker image, PyPI lychee-bin). Version and release date NOT verified.

recheck: Run all four; any one of them re-opens this verdict. (1) python tools/audit/pile.py scan --out /tmp/p.json -- if pile.py gains a check mode or a baseline ratchet, the duplicate counting in repoclear should move onto it and this component shrinks to the three small detectors. (2) Install rmlint and run it against this tree with -o json -- if its JSON output distinguishes tracked from ignored files and it gains a baseline mode, re-weigh the C-binary cost against the ~40 lines of bespoke ratchet code. (3) Fetch lychee.cli.rs -- if lychee gains bare-path (non-link) detection in prose, the stale-destination detector should be re-examined. (4) Re-run python tools/repoclear/scan.py check and python tools/audit/mutate.py --spec repoclear -- if the ratchet has never fired on a real growth since this record, its keep-ours defence weakens to the selftest, which is the standard this repo applies to everything else.
strongest_counterargument: rmlint covers duplicates AND empty dirs in one maintained binary with JSON output, and the bespoke ratchet is a small fraction of these 445 lines: the honest aggressive verdict is that the empty-dir and artifact detectors could be a thin wrapper over rmlint's JSON, and the duplicate half already is a thin wrapper over pile.py. What stops that verdict: rmlint is not git-aware, so it reports ignored and untracked noise as findings and would need an exclusion list that duplicates what the repo already maintains; it has no skill-fork semantics and no protected basenames, so it would propose deleting dot-codex/AGENTS.md; and the stale-destination detector, the part with no alternative at all, would still be bespoke. The repo is stdlib-Python-only end to end, and adding a C binary plus an install step on the self-hosted runner for a check that runs in under 2 seconds of stdlib is the wrong trade. But the counterargument stands for the day pile.py grows a check mode: then this component should shrink to the three small detectors and say so in its own record.
verdict: split: keep the ratchet, the empty-dir / artifact / stale-destination detectors, and the gate wiring; the duplicate detection stays owned by tools/audit/pile.py and is used as-is via its manifest, not re-implemented.
what_ours_does: tools/repoclear/scan.py (445 lines, stdlib only): scan (human report), check (baseline ratchet: exit 1 on growth, exit 2 on a missing baseline), selftest (planted synthetic git repo proving each detector fires). Detectors: duplicate counts read from pile.py's manifest (subprocess, no re-implementation); empty dirs by top-down filesystem walk with SKIP_DIRS + .claude/worktrees exclusion, topmost empty dir per empty subtree; tracked build artifacts by git ls-files against artifact patterns; stale prompt destinations by parsing Output-lands-in / Land-as lines in work-docs/research/prompts/*.md and requiring the destination directory to exist (sentence punctuation stripped first, because Path collapses a trailing /. one level up). Wired as the required repoclear gate domain in quality-contract.json (cmd python tools/repoclear/scan.py check), with a falsifiability step (repoclear selftest), a mutation spec (5 of 5 caught), pytest tests (10), a committed baseline, a spec doc, and a dir-purpose row.
why: night-rick#35 (Repo Clear EPIC) prescribes a checker with a gate domain, not another prose standard. The duplicate half of that checker already existed in tools/audit/pile.py (scan + selftest + mutation spec), but nothing gated on its report: only its selftest runs, in the falsifiability job. The empty-dir, tracked-artifact, and stale-prompt-destination detectors existed nowhere: pointers.py scans hooks/skills trees only, never work-docs prose, and drift.py is lane/charter drift, not repo hygiene. So the component is 445 lines of which the genuinely new detection is the three small detectors plus the baseline ratchet (check fails when any count grows past state/repoclear-baseline.json, exit 2 on a missing baseline). The duplicate counting is a subprocess call to pile.py scan plus JSONL parsing, deliberately, so there is one owner per detection. Measured on main 2026-11-07: pile reports 2 duplicate-doc groups (2 redundant copies), 19 identical skills, 38 forked skills; 0 empty dirs; 0 tracked artifacts; 15 stale prompt destinations before the fix (7 prompts x2 + README), 0 after. The baseline records exactly those numbers; collapsing the duplicate/fork backlog is follow-up work (#92 / PR #444 and a dedup unit), not this component.
